mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an easing monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the FEDFUNDS change signal falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the 20-day forward returns in months with FEDFUNDS decline are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 1.0% (a threshold indicating a tightening cycle), it increases the cost of capital for corporations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a successful monetary policy response to economic softening, boosting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with labor market strength
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction term of FEDFUNDS change and UNRATE change, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (characterized by high GDP growth and low unemployment), a sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand and corporate investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regimes, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when HOUST increases by more than 1% month-over-month, or the Rank IC for the HOUST signal in late-cycle is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market, which typically leads to higher wage growth and corporate profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the UNRATE change signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the 20-day forward returns in months with UNRATE decline are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 95 (a threshold indicating a significant slowdown in manufacturing and mining), it signals weakening economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 95, or the Rank IC for the INDPRO signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansion regimes (characterized by low unemployment and rising industrial production), a positive growth rate in real GDP (GDPC1) signals robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In early-cycle expansion regimes, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 growth is above 1.5% annualized, or the Rank IC for the GDPC1 signal in early-cycle is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates broad-based economic strength across the housing and manufacturing sectors, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction term of HOUST change and INDPRO change, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.
